title: fluctuations: three sphere sizes, three chained runs
purpose: Exercises `fluctuations` [@epsrmanual], which samples the number N of molecule centres in spheres of radius `rmax` placed at random positions in the box, the distribution of N - <N>, and the averages <N>, <N²> and S(0) = (<N²> - <N>²)/<N>, the long-wavelength limit of the structure factor, related to the isothermal compressibility [@hansenmcdonald2006]. Here three sphere sizes are accumulated over three chained runs, and the random-number state is carried from run to run.
fortran: `fluctuations.f`: `run_fluctuations` (averages, S(0), list-directed real*8 output), `find_fluctuations` (random spheres, counting)
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Spheres of radius 4, 6.5 and 10 Å, 3000 random centres each (Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992]). After the three passes the reference gives <N> = 4.454, 18.974 and 69.158 molecules and S(0) = 0.634, 0.752 and 0.938.
inputs: `numfluct.FLUCTUATIONS.dat`: `nsize 60`, `nsumt 0`, `nsamples 3000`, three sizes (`rmax` 4.0, 6.5, 10); no `randomno.dat` initially; `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: `repeat 3`: pass 1 resets the generator (no `randomno.dat`) and saves its state; passes 2 and 3 continue from `randomno.dat` and average. Compared after each pass: `numfluct.FLUCTUATIONS.n01` (accumulated N - <N> distributions), the rewritten `.dat` file with `nsumt` and the running real*8 averages `ntotal`, `nsqtotal`, `szero` written list-directed (reference after pass 3: `nsumt 3`, `ntotal 4.4543333336909612`), and `randomno.dat`. The configuration is the same in every pass, so the chained passes test the read-back of the accumulated file and the running-average arithmetic.
